source.title: Stimulus onset quenches neural variability: a widespread cortical phenomenon

confidence_rationale: Exceptionally broad and robust empirical base -- 14 datasets, seven cortical areas across four lobes, two species, replicated in membrane potential, single-unit spiking and array-measured correlated variability, awake and anaesthetised. Source quality is very high. It is filed as mixed for MECH-440 because it establishes the existence and modulation of a pre-commitment variability regime (supporting the premise that there IS a spread to modulate) while simultaneously identifying a mechanism -- input-driven stabilisation of network state -- that predicts injected variability will be QUENCHED at exactly the point MECH-440 needs it to propagate. That second reading is a candidate explanation for the V3-EXQ-708a null and is the reason this entry is decision-relevant rather than merely contextual.
failure_signatures: Variability declines at stimulus onset even when the stimulus produces little change in MEAN firing rate. So a manipulation can be demonstrably live in the mean while its variance contribution is independently suppressed -- an instrument that verifies a lever is 'reaching' the pathway by checking mean-level effects does NOT thereby show the variance survives to commitment.

The decline was observed for every stimulus tested, in every one of seven cortical areas, awake or anaesthetised -- suggesting a general property of cortex that its state is STABILISED by input. Injected noise upstream of a strongly input-driven stage should be expected to be attenuated by default, not to propagate by default.
The quenching appears in correlated variability measured across populations, not only in single units, so it is not a spike-count artefact that a population-level readout would average away.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Across 14 datasets from seven cortical areas spanning four lobes in monkeys and cats, stimulus onset caused a decline in neural response variability. This occurred even when the stimulus produced little change in mean firing rate, and was observed in membrane potential, in single-unit spiking, and in correlated spiking variability across 96-electrode arrays, regardless of whether the animal was awake, behaving or anaesthetised -- suggesting a general property of cortex, that its state is stabilised by input.
mapping.ree_translation: Two readings, both live, and they are what make this decision-relevant for MECH-440. (a) SUPPORTING: there is a real pre-commitment variability regime whose spread is high before an input arrives and collapses as the network is driven toward a decision -- i.e. the stage V3-EXQ-708a was probing genuinely exists in biology, and its spread genuinely is modulated. (b) COMPLICATING: the modulation runs the wrong way for a noise-injection lever. Cortex stabilises under drive, so variance injected into a strongly input-driven selection stage is expected to be attenuated there. If E3's selection pathway is analogous, a temperature or weight-noise term could be demonstrably live and still fail to raise committed-action entropy, not because it never reached the distribution-forming stage but because that stage actively suppresses variance.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The largest caveat is that 'stimulus onset' in sensory and premotor cortex is not the same event as 'commitment' in E3's selection pathway, and I am mapping a sensory-drive phenomenon onto a decision-commitment stage. The paper does not test action selection under uncertainty; it tests responses to stimuli, mostly in sensory areas, and the interpretive frame of state-stabilisation-by-input is the authors' proposal rather than a demonstrated mechanism. Reading it as 'the pre-commit distribution gets quenched' is an extrapolation. Additionally, variability here is spike-count/membrane-potential variance across trials, which is not the same quantity as entropy over a discrete action distribution -- MECH-440's observable is categorical entropy at argmax and there is no direct measurement correspondence. Filed as a hypothesis-generator for interpreting V3-EXQ-708b, explicitly not as evidence bearing on MECH-440's falsifier.
mapping.source_context: Macaque and cat cortex, seven areas across four lobes; extracellular single-unit, 96-electrode array, and intracellular membrane-potential recordings; awake, behaving and anaesthetised preparations.

confidence_components.notes: Source quality near ceiling -- this is one of the better-replicated phenomena in systems neuroscience. Aggregate pulled to 0.70 almost entirely by mapping: sensory-drive-onset is being mapped onto decision-commitment, and trial-to-trial rate variance onto categorical action entropy. Both are real gaps. The entry earns its place by generating a discriminating interpretation for the already-queued 708b rather than by directly evidencing the claim.
